summary: Franklin County tower of about 100 ft, erected 1954-55 and recorded as dismantled in fiscal 1974-75 by Missouri conservation reports; no source describes the site now.

facts.status_note: Dismantled, according to the Missouri Department of Conservation annual report for fiscal 1974-75, as quoted on the Central US Lookouts page. No source read describes the site now.

events.note: Recorded as newly erected in the FY 1954-55 Missouri Conservation Commission annual report. The report year is given; no exact construction date.
November 1955 Washington Missourian notice names Virgil Fritz of Spring Bluff as the Beaufort towerman; he would man the tower in dry fire season.
September 1967 St. Clair Chronicle notice: vandalism at the Beaufort fire tower cost the state more than $1000; two Union men were convicted of injuring state property.
Recorded as dismantled in the Missouri Department of Conservation annual report for fiscal 1974-75. The year is the fiscal-year report, not a confirmed date.

notes_for_editor: Single site, but four dated items: the FY 1954-55 Conservation Commission report, a November 1955 Washington Missourian notice, a September 1967 St. Clair Chronicle notice and the FY1974-75 MDC report. These are read only as quoted on the page; the newspapers and reports were not opened. The 100-foot height is converted to 30.5 m (the brief already had 30.5). The brief's point (38.3997, -91.1297) sits at the town; the tower was about three miles southwest on Highway EE, so the record point may be off by about three miles. The 1975 removal year is the fiscal-year report, not a confirmed date. Two men are named in the source; the story leaves their names out. Brief record: county and agency match the page; status 'gone' matches the page.
